before: A w:pPr or w:rPr kept its children in the order the file or a concurrent merge gave them, and a save wrote that order even when it broke the schema sequence.
after: A file opens with the modelled children of those containers in schema order, and a save writes them in schema order. A tree that a concurrent merge left out of order keeps the merged order in the tree and the shared state; only the saved bytes are reordered. The canonical fingerprint still reads the tree order.
reason: No shared field or operation changes. Replicas exchange shared state, not saved bytes, and a room seeds its shared state from one tree, so every participant sees the order that tree holds. Released and new participants keep the same meaning for shared data.
